summary: A for loop repeats a block a set number of times. Its header has three parts: start, condition, and update.
notes: let lap = 1 runs once, before the loop starts.
lap < 6 is checked before each pass. The loop stops when it is false.
lap++ adds 1 after each pass. seconds -= 2 subtracts 2.
pitfall: Writing lap <= 5 versus lap < 5 changes the count by one. Check the first and last values the loop prints.
contrast: JavaScript's counting loop uses Java's three-part header, with let instead of int. There is no range() as in Python.
